app.name: Slack
app.managed_alternative_note: Composio provides out-of-the-box Slack integration with pre-configured bot scopes and instant user-level authentication. Use Composio to bypass multi-workspace distribution review.
when_to_byoc: Custom bot branding: Custom bot display name and company icon in customer channels
Enterprise Grid: Direct deployment into customer Enterprise Grid orgs with custom admin approvals
Socket Mode / Event Subscriptions: Private WebSocket stream handling behind enterprise VPCs

summary: Instant for your own workspace. Requires formal App Directory review (2–3 weeks) only if distributing to external customer workspaces.
difficulty_factors: +25 pts: App Directory review required for multi-workspace public distribution
+10 pts: Requires valid privacy policy, support URL, and comprehensive feature description
+10 pts: Bot token vs User token permission split and strict OAuth v2 flow

time_estimate.production_wait_claim: 1–3 weeks for public Slack App Directory distribution
time_estimate.approval_wait: Instant for dev workspace; 1–3 weeks for App Directory

prerequisites: A Slack account with admin permissions in a development workspace
HTTPS redirect URL (Slack rejects plain HTTP even on local domains, except ngrok or tunneling)
Public Privacy Policy and Support URL if enabling public distribution

path.detail: Navigate to api.slack.com/apps -> Click 'Create New App' -> Choose 'From scratch' -> Enter App Name and pick Development Workspace.
Under Features -> OAuth & Permissions, scroll to Scopes. Add bot token scopes (e.g. chat:write, channels:read, app_mentions:read).
Under OAuth & Permissions -> Redirect URLs, add your HTTPS callback URL (e.g. https://agent.app/api/auth/callback/slack).

path.action: Install App to Workspace for Local Testing
path.detail: Click 'Install to Workspace' -> Grant requested permissions. You receive a Bot User OAuth Token (xoxb-...) for instant testing.
Go to Settings -> Manage Distribution -> Complete the checklist (Hardcoded URLs check, Privacy Policy, Icon). Submit to App Directory if listing publicly.

scopes.unlocks: Send messages as the agent bot into channels where invited
View basic channel names and metadata in public channels
Read conversation history in public channels

approval.what_reviewed: Only required for public distribution to non-dev workspaces. Slack reviews security, scope minimization, functional user commands, and landing page privacy policies.
typical_rejection_reasons: Over-requesting broad scopes (e.g. requesting admin or channels:history when only chat:write is needed)
Broken OAuth install button or missing error handling in callback flow
Privacy policy does not explicitly mention data retention or deletion terms
what_to_prepare: Privacy policy and terms of service hosted on a public domain
Detailed step-by-step test instructions and screencast video for the Slack review team

blockers_and_fixes.symptom: invalid_auth or not_authed when testing API methods
blockers_and_fixes.cause: Attempting to use a User token where a Bot token (xoxb) is expected, or bot not invited to the target channel.
blockers_and_fixes.fix: Invite your bot to the channel (/invite @bot_name) and pass the 'Authorization: Bearer xoxb-...' header.
blockers_and_fixes.escalation_template: N/A - Channel membership is a local workspace action.

blockers_and_fixes.cause: Public distribution has not been activated, so only the development workspace can install the app.
blockers_and_fixes.fix: In Slack App settings, go to 'Manage Distribution', verify all checklist items, and turn on public distribution.
blockers_and_fixes.escalation_template: Hello Slack Support, we submitted our app [APP_ID] for App Directory review on [DATE]. We are awaiting initial feedback regarding scope review.

agent_can_do: Draft the Slack manifest JSON with exact scopes, events, and slash commands
Generate the privacy policy and terms boilerplate needed for distribution checklist
Construct OAuth v2 code exchange handlers with workspace team ID tracking
Draft submission notes explaining each scope's business purpose for the Slack review team
you_must_do: Own or create a Slack development workspace
Accept Slack Developer Terms and click 'Install to Workspace'
Submit the public distribution application form and answer reviewer inquiries
agent_vs_human.handoff_critical_point: Agent outputs the Slack manifest JSON; human pastes into Slack App Manifest or creates app manually in api.slack.com.

what_to_do_next: Create app from manifest or scratch at https://api.slack.com/apps.
Add 'chat:write' and 'channels:read' bot scopes and install to your dev workspace.
Decide if multi-workspace distribution is required; if so, prepare privacy policy.

evidence.claim: Slack apps can be tested instantly in your development workspace without review
evidence.snippet: You can install your app to your development workspace immediately to begin testing features and interacting with the Slack Web API.

evidence.claim: Slack OAuth v2 strictly separates Bot Token Scopes from User Token Scopes
evidence.snippet: OAuth v2 granular permissions allow you to request bot scopes that apply to your bot user, and user scopes that act on behalf of the installing user.

evidence.claim: Public distribution requires review if listed in App Directory; direct install link is unreviewed if distribution enabled
evidence.snippet: Public distribution allows anyone with the direct install link to add your app. Submitting to the Slack App Directory requires a formal review process.

uncertainties: Slack App Directory review timeline is not officially committed to a fixed SLA; official docs say 'several days to a few weeks', community forums report 2–3 weeks on average.
